notes: 93-95: modern four-storey block, cream render, white bands, ground-floor arcade along the street, black iron balconies with geraniums, wall lamps on brackets.
Across from 95: Don Pio Montoya square, a pollarded plane tree with a round crown, a small wooden hut, red-brown pavement.

San Juan kalea (old part, 61-91): narrow asphalt street with no pavements; three- and four-storey terraced houses, masonry ground floors, timber-framed or rendered upper floors, wooden balconies and glazed miradors, deep eaves.
San Juan church: ashlar sandstone, pale grey-cream blocks, small windows, square belfry.
Roofs (satellite): terracotta tile, mostly hipped; a dense band of riverside trees along the Oria; steep wooded hills all around.
South bank: road with a dark wooden rail fence along the river.
2026-10-30 (Commons photos 2010-2019, PNOA orthophoto, OSM): sources and credits in docs/places/alegia.md.
Roofs (PNOA): curved clay tiles weathered to a dusty brown-red with grey lichen, darker than plain terracotta; the town hall's roof is the darkest.

Town hall (63, 18th-century baroque): square, three storeys of cool grey ashlar with rusticated quoins and a hipped roof with deep dark eaves; on the square (north-west) four round arches, a continuous iron balcony on the first floor, four single balconies above, a central pediment with the coat of arms and a clock turret with a bell spire; on the river side a five-arch loggia standing on the rubble river wall.

Zubimusu (65), west of the town hall: pale blue-grey render, dark green shutters, iron balconies with geraniums, two stone arches at the ground floor, one of them the passage to Zubi Zaharra. House 61 across the square: grey-beige pebbledash with pale stone bands and green shutters.
Town hall square (Herriko enparantza): grey granite setts laid in fan arcs with pale stone bands; pollarded plane trees, a stone fountain (Plazako iturria), benches.

Txintxarri plaza, east of the town hall by the river: a giant stone cowbell (joare) lying on rocks, a wooden culture cabin (Kabia, 2023), a wisteria pergola with terraces, green railings on the river.

Zubi Zaharra (late 17th century, restored after the 1983 flood): a narrow humpback footbridge of grey rubble and ashlar, a large and a smaller round arch, a central pier with a rounded cutwater carried up to a refuge with a cross; moss and ferns.

Riverside of 61-91: back gardens on a three-metre rubble wall with a brick coping, brick pillars and white iron railings; wooden balconies, galleries and timber framing on the river fronts; a weir just upstream of the bridge.

Church square (east of the church, at its foot): a row of pollarded plane trees, a stone fountain (Elizako iturria), planters with geraniums. The baroque portal and the belfry face east, away from the camera.
Street lamps along San Juan kalea: wall brackets painted blue with cream bowl shades. Every old house carries its name (Konfiteroenea, Kafeteroenea, Txanboliñenea...).

North-east of the town hall: San Juan kalea turns north-east towards the Kale Beheko fountain, with bars, the post office, a pharmacy and a playground with a small court (Parke ttikie). The open-air pelota court, the Santo Kristo hermitage and the station are 100-150 m beyond the map's corner.
South bank east of the road bridge: Bulebarra, a paved prow with stepped seating and a row of plane trees above the river, then the Amezketa stream joining the Oria.

Aquí empieza la calle vieja de Alegia.
